=========================================================================\n    public interface ITransformedEventDispatcher\n    {\n        Task DispatchAsync(TransformedEvent evt, CancellationToken transformed events onto a downstream\n    /// Kinesis stream.  If no stream is configured (e.g. local tests), we fall\n    /// back to logging.\n    /// </summary>\n    public sealed class FireAndForgetDispatcher : ITransformedEventDispatcher, IDisposable\n    {\n        private readonly ILogger _log;\n        private readonly IAmazonKinesis _kinesis;\n        private readonly string _targetStreamName;\n        private readonly ConcurrentQueue<Amazon.Kinesis.Model.PutRecordsRequestEntry> _buffer = new();\n\n        public FireAndForgetDispatcher(ILogger log)\n        {\n            _log              = log;\n            _kinesis          = new AmazonKinesisClient(); // region inferred from Lambda environment\n            _targetStreamName = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(\"TRANSFORMED_STREAM_NAME\") \n                                ?? \"pulseops-transformed-events\";\n        }\n\n        public Task DispatchAsync(TransformedEvent evt, CancellationToken ct)\n        {\n            var json   = JsonSerializer.Serialize(evt);\n            var record = new Amazon.Kinesis.Model.PutRecordsRequestEntry\n            {\n                PartitionKey = evt.Tags.TryGetValue(\"source\", out var source) ? source : \"unknown\",\n                Data         = new MemoryStream(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(json))\n            };\n\n            _buffer.Enqueue(record);\n\n            // Flush in background if we crossed threshold (imperfect, but keeps demo short)\n            if (_buffer.Count >= 500)\n            {\n                _ = FlushAsync(CancellationToken.None);\n            }\n\n            return Task.CompletedTask;\n        }\n\n        public async Task DeadLetterAsync(KinesisEvent.KinesisEventRecord rawRecord, Exception ex, CancellationToken ct)\n        {\n            // Pipe to DLQ – in demo we just log.  In production it’s an SQS DLQ.\n            _log.Warning(ex, \"Dead-lettering record {@PartitionKey}\", rawRecord.Kinesis.PartitionKey);\n            await Task.CompletedTask;\n        }\n\n        private async Task FlushAsync(CancellationToken ct)\n        {\n            if (_buffer.IsEmpty) return;\n\n            var batch = new List<Amazon.Kinesis.Model.PutRecordsRequestEntry>();\n            while (batch.Count < 500 && _buffer.TryDequeue(out var entry))\n            {\n                batch.Add(entry);\n            }\n\n            if (batch.Count == 0) return;\n\n            var request = new Amazon.Kinesis.Model.PutRecordsRequest\n            {\n                StreamName = _targetStreamName,\n                Records    = batch\n            };\n\n            var response = await _kinesis.PutRecordsAsync(request, ct);\n\n            if (response.FailedRecordCount > 0)\n            {\n                _log.Error(\"Failed to write {Failed}/{Total} records to stream {Stream}\",\n                           response.FailedRecordCount, batch.Count, _targetStreamName);\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                _log.Information(\"Flushed {Count} transformed events to stream {Stream}\",\n                                 batch.Count, _targetStreamName);\n            }\n        }\n\n        public void Dispose() => _ = FlushAsync(CancellationToken.None);\n    }\n}\n```","numLines":430,"startLine":1,"totalLines":430}}}

storing events inside the current active window(s)\n        // We deliberately use a ConcurrentQueue to keep insertion O(1) and avoid\n        // global locks on the hot path.\n        private readonly ConcurrentQueue<ProductivityEvent> _buffer = new();\n\n        // Latest watermark processed (monotonic)\n        private DateTimeOffset _currentWindowCutoff;\n\n        public TimeSeriesWindowAggregator(\n            KpiAggregationDelegate aggregationLogic,\n            TimeWindowOptions options,\n            int boundedCapacity = 10_000) // backpressure\n        {\n            options.Validate();\n\n            _aggregationLogic = aggregationLogic ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(aggregationLogic));\n            _options = options;\n\n            _inputChannel = Channel.CreateBounded<ProductivityEvent>(new BoundedChannelOptions(boundedCapacity)\n            {\n                SingleReader = true,\n                SingleWriter = false,\n                FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait\n            });\n\n            _currentWindowCutoff = AlignToWindowStart(DateTimeOffset.UtcNow);\n\n            _backgroundTask = Task.Factory.StartNew(\n                WorkLoopAsync,\n                _cts.Token,\n                TaskCreationOptions.LongRunning,\n                TaskScheduler.Default).Unwrap();\n        }\n\n        #region IObserver\n\n        public void OnNext(ProductivityEvent value)\n        {\n            if (!_inputChannel.Writer.TryWrite(value))\n            {\n                // backpressure fallback – should never happen due to boundedChannel Wait\n                throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Input channel rejected write unexpectedly.\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        public void OnError(Exception error)\n        {\n            // Bubble up to downstream subscribers – they'll decide what to do.\n            _metricStream.OnError(error);\n        }\n\n        public void OnCompleted()\n        {\n            _inputChannel.Writer.Complete();\n        }\n\n        #endregion\n\n        #region IObservable\n\n        public IDisposable Subscribe(IObserver<KpiMetric> observer)\n        {\n            return _metricStream.AsObservable().Subscribe(observer);\n        }\n\n        #endregion\n\n        private async Task WorkLoopAsync()\n        {\n            try\n            {\n                var reader = _inputChannel.Reader;\n\n                while (await reader.WaitToReadAsync(_cts.Token).ConfigureAwait(false))\n                {\n                    while (reader.TryRead(out var evt))\n                    {\n                        _buffer.Enqueue(evt);\n                    }\n\n                    FlushExpiredWindows();\n                }\n            }\n            catch (OperationCanceledException)\n            {\n                // Normal shutdown – ignore.\n            }\n            catch (Exception ex)\n            {\n                // Surface unexpected }\n        }\n\n        /// <summary>\n        /// Remove records that no longer belong to any open window and emit\n        /// completed windows downstream.\n        /// </summary>\n        [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]\n        private void FlushExpiredWindows()\n        {\n            var now = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;\n\n            // Move watermark forward in increments of SlideInterval until the current time is covered.\n            while (_currentWindowCutoff + _options.WindowSize <= now)\n            {\n                var windowStart = _currentWindowCutoff;\n                var windowEnd = windowStart + _options.WindowSize;\n\n                // Gather relevant events.\n                var windowEvents = DrainEvents(windowStart, windowEnd);\n\n                // Apply user-supplied aggregation delegate.\n                try\n                {\n                    foreach (var metric in _aggregationLogic(windowEvents, windowStart, windowEnd))\n                    {\n                        _metricStream.OnNext(metric);\n                    }\n                }\n                catch (Exception ex)\n                {\n                    // Fail-fast on faulty business logic so we don't silently produce wrong numbers.\n                    _metricStream.OnError(new AggregationException(\n                        $\"Aggregation delegate threw for window {windowStart:o}-{windowEnd:o}\", ex));\n                }\n\n                // Advance watermark\n                _currentWindowCutoff = windowStart + _options.SlideInterval;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /// <summary>\n        /// Retrieve and remove events from the buffer that are part of the\n        /// requested window interval.\n        /// </summary>\n        private IReadOnlyCollection<ProductivityEvent> DrainEvents(DateTimeOffset windowStart, DateTimeOffset windowEnd)\n        {\n            var set = new List<ProductivityEvent>(capacity: 1024);\n\n            while (_buffer.TryPeek(out var candidate))\n            {\n                if (candidate.Timestamp < windowStart)\n                {\n                    // Too old: discard\n                    _buffer.TryDequeue(out _);\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                if (candidate.Timestamp >= windowEnd)\n                {\n                    // Still in future window – stop draining.\n                    break;\n                }\n\n                // In window range\n                _buffer.TryDequeue(out var inWindow);\n                if (inWindow != null)\n                {\n                    set.Add(inWindow);\n                }\n            }\n\n            return set;\n        }\n\n        /// <summary>\n        /// Aligns the given timestamp to the previous aligned window boundary.\n        /// </summary>\n        private DateTimeOffset AlignToWindowStart(DateTimeOffset timestamp)\n        {\n            var ticks = (long)(_options.SlideInterval.Ticks *\n                               Math.Floor(timestamp.UtcTicks / (double)_options.SlideInterval.Ticks));\n            return new DateTimeOffset(ticks, TimeSpan.Zero);\n        }\n\n        public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()\n        {\n            _cts.Cancel();\n\n            // Wait for graceful termination, but don't block forever.\n            var completedTask = await Task.WhenAny(_backgroundTask, Task.Delay(5000)).ConfigureAwait(false);\n            if (completedTask != _backgroundTask)\n            {\n                // Force task to fault for diagnostic purposes\n                _metricStream.OnError(new TimeoutException(\"Aggregator failed to shut down in timely manner.\"));\n            }\n\n            _cts.Dispose();\n            _metricStream.Dispose();\n        }\n\n        /// <summary>\n        /// Aggregation delegate convenience builder that computes a simple\n        /// sum over NumericValue field.\n        /// </summary>\n        public static KpiAggregationDelegate SumNumeric(string metricName, Func<ProductivityEvent, bool>? predicate = null)\n            => (events, start, end) =>\n            {\n                var query = predicate is null ? events : events.Where(predicate);\n                var total = query.Sum(e => e.NumericValue.GetValueOrDefault());\n                return new[]\n                {\n                    new KpiMetric(start, end, metricName, total, DimensionKeys: null)\n                };\n            };\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Bundles aggregation related failures so they can be handled explicitly\n    /// by an upstream error boundary (e.g. Lambda DLQ).\n    /// </summary>\n    public sealed class AggregationException : Exception\n    {\n        public AggregationException(string message, Exception innerException)\n            : base(message, innerException)\n        {\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Example usage wiring in a Lambda context\n    //\n    // var options = new TimeWindowOptions\n    // {\n    //     WindowSize = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5),\n    //     SlideInterval = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)\n    // };\n Specifically:\n\n1. **The `_buffer` field** (Line 310) is a `List<MetricDataPoint>`, which is **NOT thread-safe**.\n\n2. **The `WriteAsync` method** (Lines 312-318) calls `_buffer.AddRange(metrics)`, which modifies the internal array of the List.\n\n3. **The `EventTransformationPipeline`** class (Lines 328-461) uses TPL Dataflow's `ActionBlock` with `MaxDegreeOfParallelism = maxDegreeOfParallelism` (default value: 4, as seen on Line 339).\n\n4. **When multiple threads** from the ActionBlock call `WriteAsync` concurrently, they simultaneously modify the non-thread-safe `List<T>`:\n   - Internal array resizing can cause data loss\n   - Concurrent writes to the same array indices cause data corruption\n   - The Count and internal array can become inconsistent\n\n### Why This Causes \"End of Stream\" Serialization Errors\n\nWhile the direct symptom mentioned in the task is `SerializationException: End of Stream encountered before parsing was completed`, this race condition in `MemoryMetricSink` can cause:\n\n1. **Corrupted or truncated data** being written to the buffer\n2. **Missing data** when concurrent resize operations discard partially written elements\n3. **Jumbled byte sequences** when array boundaries become inconsistent\n\nWhen downstream components attempt to deserialize data that was corrupted during the parallel write operations, they encounter incomplete or malformed byte arrays, resulting in the serialization exception.\n\n### Architectural Pattern Identified\n\nThe codebase correctly uses the **Strategy Pattern** for KPI transformations and the **Pipeline Pattern** (via TPL Dataflow) for high-throughput processing. However, the `MemoryMetricSink` violates the thread-safety contract expected by the pipeline's parallel execution model.\n\n## Implementation (Proposed Fix)\n\n### Files to Modify\n\n- `/app/project/src/module_65.txt`\n\n### Changes Required\n\nReplace the non-thread-safe `List<MetricDataPoint>` with a thread-safe `ConcurrentBag<MetricDataPoint>`:\n\n**Before (Buggy Code):**\n```csharp\npublic sealed class MemoryMetricSink : IMetricSink\n{\n    private readonly List<MetricDataPoint> _buffer = new();\n\n    public Task WriteAsync(\n        IReadOnlyCollection<MetricDataPoint> metrics,\n        CancellationToken                     cancellationToken = default)\n    {\n        _buffer.AddRange(metrics);\n        return Task.CompletedTask;\n    }\n\n    public IReadOnlyList<MetricDataPoint> Snapshot()\n        => _buffer.ToImmutableArray();\n}\n```\n\n**After (Fixed Code):**\n```csharp\n/// <summary>\n/// In-memory </summary>\npublic sealed class MemoryMetricSink : IMetricSink\n{\n    private readonly ConcurrentBag<MetricDataPoint> _buffer = new();\n\n    public Task WriteAsync(\n However, the `MemoryMetricSink` violates the thread-safety contract expected by the pipeline's parallel execution model.\n\n## Implementation (Proposed Fix)\n\n### Files to Modify\n\n-
